diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theoretical analysis confirmed the convergence of the RCTZFIF to to the original data-generating function.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the analysis establishes convergence of phi_epsilon to the classical RCTFIF phi and to the data-generating function psi. The only formal result, Theorem thm:convergence, is an error bound whose signature-dependent term (||epsilon||_infty/(1-|lambda|_infty))(C*Phi + 4h*eta/pi) does not tend to zero as h -> 0: no hypothesis drives ||epsilon||_infty in {0,1}, Phi = max|f_j|, or |lambda|_infty to zero, and the lambda-dependent term likewise persists for fixed scalings. Hence, even taken at face value, the bound shows a non-vanishing gap for every nontrivial signature (all experiments use epsilon = (1,...,1)), so neither convergence to phi nor to psi is established; the bound's derivation is moreover invalid (see the separate thm:convergence issues).

failure_location.quote: Rigorous error analysis is presented to establish the convergence of the proposed zipper fractal interpolants to the underlying classical fractal functions, and subsequently, to the data-generating function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract and conclusion to claim only the derived error bounds, noting that the signature-dependent and lambda-dependent terms do not vanish in general; alternatively, add hypotheses (vanishing scalings plus a corrected signature-term estimate of the right order in h) under which convergence actually follows.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's headline guarantee -- convergence of the zipper interpolants to the classical FIF and to the data-generating function -- is unsupported; the abstract and conclusion misrepresent what Section 4 proves.
issues.title: Abstract and conclusion claim convergence of RCTZFIFs that the paper's own error bound does not establish
issues.why_classification: The correction withdraws a centrally advertised promise that the mathematics does not deliver -- a limited but real loss of claimed content beyond a routine local fix; no formal theorem must be abandoned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $L_j : I \rightarrow I_j$, be the affine map given by $L_{j,\epsilon}(t) = a_i t + b_j, j \in \mathbb{N}_{n-1}$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: The horizontal scaling and offset of the zipper IFS maps are defined from the data values f_j and the symbols y_n, y_1, which are never defined anywhere in the paper, instead of from the knots t_j. As written, a_j and b_j are undefined; taken literally as f-based quantities they would not satisfy the required endpoint conditions L_{j,epsilon}(t_1) = t_{j+epsilon_j}, L_{j,epsilon}(t_n) = t_{j+1-epsilon_j} mapping I onto I_j. The formulas forced by those endpoint conditions are a_j = (t_{j+1-epsilon_j} - t_{j+epsilon_j})/(t_n - t_1) and b_j = (t_n t_{j+epsilon_j} - t_1 t_{j+1-epsilon_j})/(t_n - t_1).

failure_location.quote: a_j = \frac{f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-f_{j+\epsilon_j}}{y_n - y_1}, b_j = \frac{f_n f_{j+\epsilon_j}-f_1 f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}}{f_n - y_1}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the f/y-based formulas by the knot-based ones forced by the stated endpoint conditions (and fix the a_i/a_j index slip in the map definition); no downstream argument needs to change.
issues.overall_effect: The IFS maps L_{j,epsilon}, and hence the entire RCTZFIF construction, are not well-defined as written; every later use of a_j (contraction conditions, positivity bounds, convergence estimates, the numerical scaling bounds) presupposes the corrected knot-based definition.
issues.title: Zipper horizontal maps are ill-defined: a_j and b_j are built from data values f and undefined symbols y_n, y_1 instead of knots t
issues.why_classification: The correction is essentially forced by the stated endpoint conditions and is local; all constructions, theorems, and the advertised scope survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\phi$ denotes the rational cubic trigonometric FIF. \cite{chand2015positivity}

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation subtracts the self-referential equations of phi_epsilon and phi as if both held at the same argument with the same subinterval map. But phi is the classical RCTFIF, whose maps L_j are orientation-preserving, while for epsilon_j = 1 the zipper map reverses orientation (a_j < 0 and L_{j,epsilon}(t) = L_j(t_1+t_n-t) != L_j(t)); thus phi_epsilon(L_{j,epsilon}(t)) - phi(L_j(t)) is not a value of phi_epsilon - phi at a common point, so the displayed identity -- hence the recursion and the bound ||phi_epsilon - phi|| <= ||M_{j,epsilon} - M_j||/(1-|lambda|_infty) -- does not follow. The bound is in fact false: with three knots, constant data f = (c,c,c), slopes (d_1, d, d) with d != 0, and signature (0,1), the zipper endpoint data coincide with the classical ones, so M_{j,epsilon} = M_j for all j and the bound forces phi_epsilon = phi; yet combining the two fixed-point equations on the reversed segment yields lambda[phi(1-t) - phi(t)] = M_2(t) - M_2(1-t), which fails at first order near t = 0 unless d = 0, so phi_epsilon != phi. The comparison also silently assumes phi is built with the same scaling factors and shape parameters as phi_epsilon (phi is not even defined in the statement of thm:convergence).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive ||phi_epsilon - phi|| via a valid argument, e.g., comparing the Read-Bajraktarevic operators T_epsilon and T_0 (both sup-norm contractions with ratio |lambda|_infty), which yields a comparable bound plus an additional term |lambda_j| * sup_t |phi(t) - phi(t_1+t_n-t)| for reversed segments; also state explicitly that phi shares the scaling factors and shape parameters of phi_epsilon.
issues.overall_effect: The zipper-specific first term of Theorem thm:convergence -- its only new content beyond the classical RCTFIF bound -- is unproven and its derivation route is refuted; the theorem is unsupported for every non-classical signature, including the epsilon = (1,...,1) used in all experiments.
issues.title: Core comparison step of the convergence proof is invalid (and false) for reversed segments epsilon_j = 1
issues.why_classification: A contained re-derivation with standard fixed-point machinery preserves a recognizably comparable error bound (same decomposition, an extra lambda-amplified term, no rate loss), so the loss is limited; but the paper's central comparison step is falsified and cannot be patched locally.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $h_j = la_j$, and by Theorem \ref{thm:rctfif}, we get

issues.failure_explanation: The quantitative estimate fails in several independent ways: (i) upper-balling ||X/q_{j,epsilon}(theta)|| by ||X||/xi requires xi to be a lower bound for |q|, but xi is defined as a maximum of |q_j(theta)| (with the ill-formed index '1 <= j,epsilon <= n-1'); (ii) the constant C := q_{j,epsilon}(theta)/xi appearing in the statement of Theorem thm:convergence depends on the free variables j and theta, so the stated bound is ill-defined; (iii) the upper-bound chain illegally retains negative terms ('-(2l*delta*a_j*B_2)/(pi*xi)*||d_{j+1-epsilon_j} - d_{j+1}||' and the bracket '[alpha*B_1 - delta*B_2]'), which is invalid for sup-norm upper bounds; (iv) the step |f_{j+epsilon_j} - f_j| <= Phi fails for sign-changing data (a factor 2 is needed; no positivity is hypothesized in this section), and Phi omits f_n; (v) h_j = l*a_j is negative for reversed segments, so '4h_j/pi' is not a valid magnitude; (vi) Theorem thm:rctfif is invoked at this step although it bounds ||psi - phi||, not ||M_{j,epsilon} - M_j||.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the estimate: take xi as a positive lower bound of |q_{j,epsilon}| over j and theta in [0, pi/2], define C as a genuine constant (e.g., the max over j, theta of (alpha*B_0 + beta*B_1 + gamma*B_2 + delta*B_3)/xi), replace the negative terms by absolute values, use |f_{j+epsilon_j} - f_j| <= 2*Phi (or add a positivity hypothesis), and use |h_j|; a bound of the same structural form survives with adjusted constants.
issues.overall_effect: The bound on ||M_{j,epsilon} - M_j|| and, with it, the explicit constants and the stated form of the first term of Theorem thm:convergence are unreliable; the theorem as printed cannot be applied.
issues.title: Ill-defined constants xi (a maximum of |q|) and C = q/xi, plus invalid inequality steps, in the error-bound derivation
issues.why_classification: Repairing requires redoing the inequality chain and redesigning the theorem's constants (several independent invalid steps with non-forced choices of repair), which is more than a routine local fix, but a comparable bound of the same form survives without new proof architecture or rate loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and $|\lambda_j| < a_j, j\in \mathbb{N}_{n-1}$ is the vertical scaling factor

By Theorem \ref{existence_of_rationalFIF}, the fixed point of the IFS $\{I\times K; (L_{j,\epsilon}(t), F_{j,\epsilon}(t,f)), j\in \mathbb{N}_{n-1}\}$ will be a graph of a $\mathcal{C}^1-$rational cubic trigonometric Fractal Interpolation Function.

issues.failure_explanation: With the knot-based definition forced by the endpoint conditions, a_j = (t_{j+1-epsilon_j} - t_{j+epsilon_j})/(t_n - t_1) is negative whenever epsilon_j = 1 (the map reverses orientation). Condition 1 of Theorem thm:positivity then requires 0 <= lambda_j < a_j < 0, which is impossible; likewise the construction hypothesis |lambda_j| < a_j is unsatisfiable, and Theorem existence_of_rationalFIF -- invoked to guarantee the C^1 FIF -- is stated only for orientation-preserving maps (its a_i = (x_{i+1}-x_i)/(x_n-x_1) > 0), so it cannot cover reversed segments. As stated, the positivity theorem is vacuous for every signature containing a 1, i.e., for all non-classical zipper signatures, including the epsilon = (1,...,1) used throughout the experiments. The numerical section contradicts the theorem as written: for the given data with epsilon = (1,...,1), a_1 = (t_1 - t_2)/(t_n - t_1) = -2/15 < 0, yet it states that Theorem thm:positivity prescribes lambda_1 in [0, 0.1333] = [0, |a_1|], showing that |a_j| was intended.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace a_j by |a_j| in the construction's contraction condition and in condition 1 of Theorem thm:positivity (also fixing the a_i -> a_j index slip), and justify existence of the C^1 zipper FIF via the Read-Bajraktarevic fixed-point argument for zipper maps (|lambda_j| < |a_j| together with the stated C^1 join conditions) rather than the classical-only Theorem existence_of_rationalFIF.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's main positivity guarantee is inapplicable, as stated, to every reversed segment (all nontrivial zipper signatures); the C^1 existence claim for the zipper IFS is likewise unestablished under the stated hypotheses.
issues.title: Positivity condition 0 <= lambda_j < min{a_i, ...} is unsatisfiable for reversed segments (a_j < 0 when epsilon_j = 1)
issues.why_classification: The absolute-value fix is local and the method, conclusion, rate, and advertised scope survive (the numerical section already uses |a_j|); but as stated the main theorem is empty for the paper's central regime, and the repair must also supply a valid existence argument for reversed segments -- a contained nontrivial addition.

Thus, ensuring the above inequalities guarantees that $p_{j,\epsilon}(\theta) > 0$, and hence, by Equation~\eqref{pos_con}, the interpolant $\phi_\epsilon$ remains strictly positive on $[t_1, t_n]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's goal is phi_epsilon > 0 on [t_1, t_n], but its central reduction assumes phi_epsilon >= 0 on [t_1, t_n] -- exactly what is to be proved -- so the argument is circular as written. The missing (standard) step is a fixed-point iteration: the zipper Read-Bajraktarevic operator T (of the type in Theorem thm:added-1) maps the cone of non-negative continuous functions with boundary values f_1, f_n > 0 into itself whenever lambda_j >= 0 and M_{j,epsilon} > 0 on I; starting from a non-negative interpolant of the positive data (e.g., the piecewise-linear one), all iterates are non-negative and converge uniformly to phi_epsilon, and then phi_epsilon = T(phi_epsilon) with M_{j,epsilon} > 0 and lambda_j >= 0 yields phi_epsilon > 0.

failure_location.quote: Assuming $\phi_\epsilon(t) \geq 0$ for all $t \in [t_1, t_n]$ and $0 \leq \lambda_j < 1$, it suffices to ensure that the rational term $\frac{p_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)}{q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)}$ is strictly non-negative over the interval.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the standard iterate/limit argument in place of the circular assumption (a few sentences using the contraction operator already introduced in Section 2).
issues.overall_effect: The conclusion of Theorem thm:positivity is not established by the given proof (the statement itself is fine once the other defects are repaired).
issues.title: Positivity proof is circular: it assumes phi_epsilon >= 0 on [t_1, t_n] in order to prove phi_epsilon > 0
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is short, local, and routine in the fractal-interpolation literature; every claim and guarantee of the theorem survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:convergence hypothesizes gamma_{j,epsilon} >= delta_{j,epsilon} (a condition inherited from the quoted RCTFIF error bound). The paper fixes delta_{j,epsilon} = 1, but the Figure 1a row of Table 2 lists gamma = [0.5, 0.5, 0.5868, 0.5221, 0.5, 0.5] (indeed gamma < 1 in every row of the table). Hence the hypothesis fails in all six subintervals and the parameter values do not satisfy Theorem thm:convergence; the sentence asserting they do is false.
